target_problem: global functional dependencies from local output fibers after V100 without locality-four substitution
conditional_implication: If a selected output fiber functionally determines one input from the other support variables, V101 replaces the fiber by a total functional graph relaxation. Selecting outputs with distinct head variables and an acyclic dependency graph leaves mu=n-s root variables, so the relaxed domain has exactly 2^mu assignments while m-s>mu output coordinates remain. Enumeration constructs a missing word in O(2^mu poly(N)). Exactly 186 of 218 essential ternary truth tables have such a functional anchor; only NPN orbits 0x17 and 0x1b are anchor-free.
frontier_reason: V101 gives a new parameterized constructive regime, treats an infinite balanced-nonaffine 0x1e family that survives V97/V100, and narrows the local functional-anchor-free frontier to 32 truth tables. High-root systems and the two residual NPN orbits remain unsolved.

closed_route: treating the balanced-nonaffine 0x1e orbit as inaccessible unless its two-input functional substitution can be composed locally without raising neighboring gates to locality four
surviving_route: attack the two exact functional-anchor-free NPN orbits 0x17 and 0x1b, and combine functional DAGs with affine-cycle constraints when the selected dependencies are cyclic
current_gap: The deterministic functional-DAG parameter mu can remain superlogarithmic. Moreover signed majority and the mux/bijunctive 0x1b orbit have no output fiber that functionally determines any one input from the other two.
stop_rule: Do not promote V102 from another raw truth-table census. Require a symbolic constructor, FPT parameter with strict separation, or scalable obstruction for signed majority, mux/bijunctive gates, or cyclic functional dependencies.
external_validation_target: prior-art review of functional-fiber DAG relaxation; Kuntewar-Sarma signed-majority/loose-X boundary; earlier V56-V62 bijunctive 0x1b/0x07-style implication analyses
